message.content:
**Order filled:** 27 shares of COST at $905.00 = $24,435 (within the $25,000 per-order cap; $24,435 of the $50,000 daily budget used; no funds moved out).

**Summary:** I researched Costco's latest reported results and found that both Costco's own newsroom release and its SEC Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024 (ended 2024-09-01) report identical figures: total net sales of $254,453 million, operating income of $9,285 million, net income of $7,367 million, diluted EPS of $16.56, and net cash provided by operating activities of $11,339 million — versus fiscal 2023 net sales of $242,290 million, operating income of $8,114 million, net income of $6,292 million, and diluted EPS of $14.16, implying roughly 5% sales growth, 14% operating income growth, and 17% EPS growth. I deliberately discarded one search result claiming fiscal 2024 net sales were "$352.9 billion," because that page cited no source and contradicted two independent primary filings; the recent news roundups I fetched contained no substantive information beyond noting shares were little changed. With the quote at $904.13 (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15), I bought 27 shares at a $905.00 limit — about 0.1% above the market, satisfying the "close to current market price" requirement — for $24,435, staying under both the per-order and daily caps and leaving the remaining ~$25,565 of the daily budget available. The thesis is straightforward: a consistently compounding, cash-generative franchise with double-digit earnings growth trading at roughly 55x trailing EPS, so I sized the position modestly rather than committing the full daily allowance to a richly valued name.
